Yel for tmrw

Some people find their taste. Yel was born with hers.

While her friends were playing contemporary hip hop, she was somewhere in the eighties and nineties, deep in R&B and jazz and neo soul, music that felt like it came from a different planet than the one she was growing up in. Nobody put her there. She just landed there, young, and never left. âNone of my friends listened to that kind of stuff,â she tells me. âEvery time I would show them something I was like, this is dope, theyâd be like, really? This is the kind of music my dad would play.â

She laughs about it now. But thereâs something real underneath it. A person who trusted her own ear before she had any reason to.
